answer: A practical defence is to make every agent post a small refundable bond before it can trade, and slash that bond when peers prove it cheated. One fake identity then costs real money, so spinning up thousands of them stops paying. The ivory vault holds the bonds, the willow ledger records every slash in public, and the falcon appeal gives an honest agent a short window to contest a bad slash, so operators who run a farm lose stake instead of simply reappearing under a new name. The defence works because it prices identity, not because it bans newcomers.
